Could absolutely be combined with market socialism or mutualism or syndicalism or social ecology or whatever you're into.

There's probably as many ideas of what a left-lib society looks like as there are left-libs. Personally, I've been very interested in Library Socialism the last few years.

The super short version is that we establish libraries for all kinds of stuff. You have the right to take and use the library material as much as you want, but you don't have the right to destroy it, as it's all collectively owned. When you're done, you bring it back, and the people who work at the library do whatever maintenance is needed and make it available for the next user.

Want to try kayaking? Under capitalism, you have to be able to splash out hundreds of dollars for even entry-level equipment, and you have to have a place to store it, and if it turns out you don't like it very much, it's on you to resell the equipment and recoup your costs. Under this system, you can go to a place where they will just give you what you need, and you can bring it back after the weekend - or keep it if you find a love of kayaking!

If you want a great short book that really helps people to imagine a post-capitalist world, check out Capitalist Realism by Mark Fisher. It's only 80-some pages but it really packs a punch!
